name: Lael
overview: Lael is a male member of the tribe of Levi, noted primarily for being the father of Eliasaph. His mention in Scripture is brief but establishes his role within the Levitical lineage. There are no additional notes or significant events recorded about him beyond this paternal connection.
namesAndTitles: The name Lael means '[belonging] to G-d [El],' reflecting a theophoric element that acknowledges God's presence or ownership. This meaning highlights a connection to God inherent in his name, though it was not given directly by God according to the record.
familyAndRelationships: Lael is explicitly identified as a descendant of Gershon, situating him within a specific Levitical family branch. He is also noted as the father of Eliasaph, establishing a direct paternal relationship important for genealogical records.
scriptureSignificance: Lael's significance lies in his position within the Levitical genealogies, serving as a link in the lineage of Gershon's descendants. His identification as the father of Eliasaph connects him to the organization and duties of the Levites, who played a vital role in the worship and service of God. Though not prominent in narrative events, his mention preserves the continuity of God's appointed priestly tribe.
